items.title: Are Delivery Robots Scanning You Into a Database Scarier Than Flock? Et tu, ramen messenger?
items.content:
For all the controversy they’ve caught this year, Flock cameras only collect and store license plate data from passing vehicles.

But the WALL-E-esque delivery robots now trundling through America’s cities are bristling with cameras and sensors that help them navigate the bustling world around them as they make their way to customers’ doorsteps — and according to a pair of new lawsuits, you might be coughing up sensitive data in exchange for your dinner.

According to reporting by the Associated Press , delivery robot companies Coco Robotics and Serve Robotics have been hit with similar lawsuits from Chicago residents claiming that their bots are illegally collecting sensitive biometric data.

The lawsuits claim that the robots have used embedded cameras and LIDAR sensors to record information about Chicago residents’ hands, bodies, and faces as they approach their deliveries. In both cases, the plaintiffs allege that they didn’t request or consent to a robot delivery. Because they didn’t ask for a robot delivery, they argue, they certainly didn’t consent to being recorded or their data being collected by the delivery machines.

The plaintiff in the case against Coco further also alleges that a remote human operator watched his delivery as it happened. The plaintiff in the case against Serve, meanwhile, claims that the delivery robot he encountered collected and retained his data as he collected his Uber Eats order. His lawsuit also raises the concern that the data could be used to train AI or handed to third parties.

Both companies have disputed the claims. Coco, saying that privacy is a top priority, told the AP that the litigation against it is “frivolous,” and that “this lawsuit fundamentally misunderstands our technology, we have not collected biometric data in Chicago.”

“The data we share is navigational data used to make sidewalks safer for all users,” Coco told the AP . “For example, we provide real-time sidewalk hazard information to BlindSquare, a navigation app built for people who are blind or have low vision. We do not share data from the beginning or end of delivery trips under our data sharing partnerships. Privacy and compliance with the law are top priorities in everything we do.”

Serve, for its part, told the AP that it plans to “defend against” the legal action.

“Serve does not use that data to identify individuals and our systems are not designed to identify individuals or create biometric profiles,” Serve’s statement continued, per the report.

Illinois has uniquely strong laws against the nonconsensual collection of biometric data , so it’s not surprising to see cases like these brought in Chicago. As Gizmodo notes , Chicago has also seen a surge of the delivery bots over the past few years, causing frustration and annoyance among many in the city.

Regardless of how the cases shake out, the fact remains: the more automated our lives are, the more likely it is that sensitive information — about our lives and behaviors, and even our bodies — is going to be swallowed up, stored somewhere, and used in ways that we have no control over.

items.title: OpenLDK: Bringing the Java World into Common Lisp
items.summary: java, lisp
items.content:
Many years ago I worked on an alternate Java compiler and runtime

called gcj, the GNU Compiler for the Java Programming Language.

These days, my preferred programming language for most tasks is

Common Lisp, but I’m still interested in Java runtimes.

Back in late 2024, I wanted to use a Java library from SBCL, but

couldn’t find an integration approach that suited the application.

This led me to explore the idea of building a simple JVM bytecode

processor in Lisp so I could execute the code directly in process.

I started before coding agents became useful for this kind of work,

and wrote the first working version by hand.

runtime for Java, written in Common Lisp. It reads Java bytecode,

translates it into Lisp, and lets SBCL compile that Lisp into native

machine code. Java objects live in the same process and heap as the

My goal is to make Java libraries feel at home in Common Lisp. For

general Java execution, HotSpot will be much faster.

In the last few days, however, OpenLDK has gotten much better. I’ve

experimented with JVM-hosted languages and Spring Boot application

OpenLDK leads to some wonderfully strange possibilities. Java classes

become CLOS classes. Lisp can add methods around methods written in

Kotlin. A Clojure function can become something you pass to

funcall . Java’s own compiler runs inside SBCL. And an initialized

Spring Boot application can be saved in a Lisp image and launched

to a Spring Boot application running on OpenLDK, inspect its objects,

and monkey-patch its behavior while it keeps running.

Here is a tour of how it works, what it can do, and what that startup number actually means.

The compilation pipeline begins with ordinary class files. OpenLDK targets JDK 25 and uses OpenJDK’s runtime libraries, reading them from the JDK’s JMOD files or its lib/modules container.

When a class loads, OpenLDK creates its CLOS representation and installs stubs for its methods. Calling a method for the first time triggers compilation: bytecode becomes an intermediate representation, then Lisp, then native code through SBCL. The compiled definition replaces the stub.

That laziness matters. Loading a library does not mean compiling every method in it. Much of a large library may never be used by a particular application.

Stripped of the generated control-flow scaffolding and exception machinery, its translated body amounts to:

The signed-field operation preserves Java’s 32-bit integer overflow behavior. With typed operands, SBCL can compile this to a machine addition. OpenLDK handles Java’s semantics while drawing on the compiler SBCL already provides.

The translation also makes the program accessible to Lisp. Java fields become slots. Instance methods become methods of CLOS generic functions, identified by their JVM signatures so overloaded methods remain distinct. Static methods become ordinary Lisp functions. Java’s exception hierarchy has a corresponding Lisp condition hierarchy.

Compiled methods are retained in a persistent code cache. Subsequent runs can load cached code when the classes it depends on remain unchanged, and cache entries are separated by OpenLDK build. Different images can reuse compiled JDK methods too.

The most interesting consequences appear when an application starts using these representations directly.

Foreign source can appear directly inside Lisp source. After starting the relevant languages and enabling OpenLDK’s source syntax, a Kotlin expression looks like this:

$n passes the Lisp value into the Kotlin code as an object. Lexical variables, collections, and callbacks can cross the boundary without being serialized into source strings.

The same mechanism supports Scala, Groovy, Clojure, Kawa, JScheme, and ABCL. Each block keeps the language’s own syntax. Clojure also has a #[ ... ] notation.

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.title: Cybersecurity bounty hunter says Samsung TVs use AI to record audio and screenshots for ads — 'Finally found a company that truly listens to its customers,' says hacker
items.content:
Reverse engineer and cybersecurity bounty hunter log4j recently found they were getting “weirdly targeted ads” on their Samsung TV and discovered privacy breaches. As they live-tweeted their discoveries, they found increasingly concerning code in the Tizen operating system, including detailed user telemetry from packet logging, audio categorization, screenshots, cross-device identification for ad tracking, and more, all designed to extract as much user information as possible to improve targeted ads.

log4j posted on X that they were concerned with how specific the ads on their 2025 Samsung TV were. They decided to reverse-engineer the Tizen OS on their TV to see what it was doing—they “discovered PRIVACY HORROR,” log4j states, marking the start of subsequent posts sharing more concerning findings.

i own a relatively new (2025) samsung tv.

i tried reversing the firmware but it was aes encrypted and no keys unless tear it apart and do uart/jtag magic.

zero days it is. root shell on new samsung TVs!

discovered PRIVACY HORROR. write up? https://t.co/EsxxCy1b6a October 21, 2026

The tester theorizes that Samsung TVs are so sluggish because they do a lot of post-processing of user data, including audio, screenshots, and AID (a cross-device tracking ID for ads), plus computer vision processing and models running on the TV. The hacker even found a region-specific convolutional neural network (an AI) that tracks user behavior, citing examples like what videos the user watches, which ads are skipped, and video progress. Log4j also found behavior for TVs without microphones, stating it will find connected devices with microphones, such as a soundbar or a connected Bluetooth device, to record audio.

Hugging Face engineer ngxson commented that they would test the microphone behavior using their Flipper Zero and found that the TV opened the microphone for five seconds, then stopped. ngxson waited for another microphone response but found none hours later. However, ngxson explained that their Tizen TV was already rooted and had multiple settings disabled, so an unmodified TV may behave differently.

What hardware deals are you hoping to pick up during Black Friday?

The hacker used OpenAI tools to hack the TV, but the company eventually banned them for cyber abuse, as stated in an email they received. log4j defended themselves, saying they never used OpenAI’s tools to exploit or find vulnerabilities, only for local reverse engineering, and that they didn't breach the terms of use. In a comment below their post about the ban, log4j said it seemed OpenAI banned their account because of a primitive classifier.

@log4j Ok so right off the bat, it opens the mic for exactly 5 seconds then stop. Seems like a strange way to test mic (?)

Then no more recording since then, but need to keep observing more to conclude https://t.co/PSHIfMG2oO October 23, 2026

However, Samsung TVs and Tizen aren’t the only culprits in reportedly breaching user privacy; other brands like LG have also been accused of spying on customers . Many owners have also reported their TVs slowing down despite no new features or heavy apps running, suspecting it is mainly bloatware, but it could also be the spying behavior Log4j found. The hacker is also working on a comprehensive write-up of their findings, including how others could do it themselves.

At the end of the post series, they jokingly say they “finally found a company that truly listens to its customers.”

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

제가 보기에는 블랙해커들 보다는 서버측이 클라이언트의 행동을 분석하는 과정처럼 보이더군요..

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Why I Am a Programmer
items.content:
There they sit, the preschooler class encircling their mentor, the substitute teacher.

"Now class, today we will talk about what you want to be when you grow up. Isn't that fun?"

The teacher looks around and spots the child, silent, apart from the others and deep in thought.

she encourages him. Jonny looks around, confused, his train of thought disrupted. He collects himself, and stares at the teacher with a steady eye.

he says, his words becoming stronger and more confidant as he speaks.

"I want to write something that will change peoples perception of reality. I want them to walk away from the computer dazed, unsure of their footing and eyesight. I want to write something that will reach out of the screen and grab them, making heartbeats and breathing slow to almost a halt. I want to write something that, when it is finished, they are reluctant to leave, knowing that nothing they experience that day will be quite as real, as insightful, as good. I want to write demos."

Silence. The class and the teacher stare at Jonny, stunned. It is the teachers turn to be confused. Jonny blushes, feeling that something more is required.

"Either that or I want to be a fireman."

I grew up in a pre-mainstream Internet world. A time when only a handful of kids at my primary school had a computer. We lived in a rough neighbourhood and so having a computer meant that you were a target for robbery. As we all knew somebody who had their computer stolen at least once, having a computer was kept on the low down. But we still found each other. Each time word got out that some kid got a new computer, they was suspiciously quizzed before being let into our digital posse.

A lot of my childhood was spend living indoors behind a buzzing 14" CRT, pirating games with other kids via 3.5" single-density floppies with their corners drilled out, and once in a while even playing them. But I was more of a collector than gamer. Like Ash from Pokemon - got to catch them all. And the people who created computer games were my idols. I was always in awe of what they could do with that big, heavy, beige box under the table.

One day word spread that there was a way to edit saved game files via XTreeGold's Hex View that gave you unlimited lives and allowed you to skip stages. With each new game that came out, the race was on to see who could be the first to flip the right bits to get the powerups. It was seriously heart pumping. Although only tinkering, it felt like we were our own gods.

We bought a modem a few years later and soon after got a copy of The Australian BBS Listing - a textfile containing most of the publically accessible BBSes online. I dialed every one of them (but that's for another blog post). It opened up a whole new world to explore. Instead of just a handful of kids pirating games via Sneakernet, I was connected to the digital underground - a world where anything digital was within reach (some even had Internet gateways). Even the newest blockbusters that I had only read about in PC Zone magazine were all there for me to leech. All of them, soon slowly trickling down the wire via ZMODEM.

But there was something different with these BBS downloaded games. Not something bad, but something exciting. Each time these games were run, it was like a short commercial was played before the title screen. Now I'm not talking about commercials selling steak knives. Instead, these were brazen posters screaming fuck you by the people who had managed to crack the game's copy protection code and were now distributing the game illegally for free. I later found out that these commercials were called cracktros. The precursor to demos and what started the whole demoscene. But simply calling them demos just doesn't give them justice. items.title: Building Java ME Apps with Modern Tooling
items.summary: java, retrocomputing
items.content:
Java ME (Micro Edition, also referred to as J2ME) is a platform for running Java applications on small resource constrained devices, such as feature phones from before the iPhone era. It is largely considered a dead platform with the advent of smartphones, and modern feature phones such as KaiOS use web technologies instead for their apps.

However it is likely that you or someone you know have one of these old phones lying around, and you may be interested in how you can make Java apps that will run on it. This post goes through how to build a simple Java ME app solely with modern tooling in a modern environment, without needing anything from the old Sun Java ME SDKs.

The instructions in this blog post assume a Linux-y terminal environment, but you could also follow along with Git Bash or a similar environment on Windows.

Here is a simple Hello World MIDlet that we will use. It will show a simple form using the LCDUI API with the text “Hello World!”:

We will compile this with javac , but we first need the stub JARs from MicroEmulator available in the lib directory. Extract cldcapi11.jar and midpapi20.jar and put them in a lib directory next to the src directory.

The cldcapi11.jar provides the CLDC 1.1 API and midpapi20.jar provides the MIDP 2.0 API . MIDP 2.0 is circa 2002, and is probably what you want to use for widest compatibility, while it has some important features that MIDP 1.0 lacks.

Then we can compile the Java source file with the following command:

(To compile multiple .java files in src , you would put $(find src -name "*.java") instead.)

MIDlets need some metadata in the META-INF manifest file to work. Most of the fields are self-explanatory:

For the MIDlet-1 field, the format is a comma-separated list of three values: The human-readable name of the MIDlet, the path to the icon inside of the JAR, and the fully qualified class name of the entrypoint class. Since the above Java code specifies no package, it will be in the default package at the root of the JAR.

Save this to resources/META-INF/MANIFEST.MF , creating a resources/ directory to house assets to put in the final JAR. Also put a 16x16 PNG icon in resources/icon.png . Then let’s package everything together into a JAR:

Now we have a JAR file build/input.jar … But we need to preverify it before it can be run on a Java ME device.

Preverification is a process required for the KVM (the minimal Java virtual machine used in Java ME) to ensure that the bytecode is valid. Traditionally this would be done by a preverify tool from the original Java ME SDK, but ProGuard supports doing the same thing and is more modern.

You can also use ProGuard to shrink, optimise and obfuscate your code to reduce the footprint of the resulting JAR, which is especially important for Java ME apps where the JAR size limit can be very strict. But for this example we disable all of that for now and just specify -microedition to do the preverification.

Now you have a app.jar file that can actually be run on a Java ME device or in an emulator. You can use MicroEmulator to run it, or something with more features like FreeJ2ME-plus , currently the best J2ME emulator for desktop platforms.

Now that you have gotten it running in an emulator it would be nice to get it running on the real hardware. The feature phone I had lying around that’s the most functional is the Sony Ericsson S312, a budget feature phone from 2009. It even has a camera!

Java feature phones tend to have connectivity and storage mediums that are generally considered obsolete nowadays. My Sony Ericsson S312 has a proprietary charger cable with no USB on either end - supposedly you can use a special USB transfer cable, but that was a separate accessory that doesn’t seem worthwhile to obtain. In addition to this, the physical external memory storage is some strange card format that is distinct from any standard kind of SD card (M2 memory stick, not to be confused with the M.2 connector).

Update 5: Instagram is now leaking recovery email and phone numbers linked to an account.

Seems like every day a new security issue crops up at Instagram.

Instagram Exposing Linked Email and Phone Number

Update 4: A new report suggests that Instagram accounts may be vulnerable to coordinated mass-report abuse. According to the claim, when a newly created account is routed through a Los Angeles-based VPN and then submits a specific mix of reports in scam and fraud category, the targeted account can allegedly be banned without any human review.

Instagram Account Banning by AI by Reporting Scam and Fraud (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 3: Meta’s apparent fix for the AI bot vulnerability is difficult to take seriously. Instead of fully disabling the risky functionality, they reportedly removed it from the visible interface while leaving the underlying API endpoint accessible. Hiding the button may stop regular users from seeing the feature, but it does nothing if attackers can still reach the same workflow directly through the API.

Meta Hid AI Chatbot from UI (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 2: Yet another Instagram account-takeover trick is reportedly being abused, this time involving Meta’s AI chatbot. Sellers are allegedly using modified Instagram builds on Android emulators like BlueStacks, then manipulating the AI with hidden characters and carefully worded prompts to force username changes. The method is reportedly being used to grab rare OG handles, including one-letter usernames, and handle-monitoring bots have already flagged several suspicious swaps.

New Instagram AI Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

New Instagram Unpatched Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

Allegedly, the new method is via Facebook recovery. Apparently, prompting Meta AI to turn on “Development Mode” and attaching proof of account compromise along with email works. More details awaited.

There’s a version of this story where it reads like a hypothetical from a conference talk. An AI agent with elevated backend privileges. A natural language interface sitting in front of account-level APIs. No hard authentication gate before executing state changes. Someone in the audience raises their hand and says, “that’s a disaster waiting to happen.” Everyone nods.

That hypothetical played out in production over the weekend.

A logical flaw in Meta’s AI-powered Instagram account recovery assistant let attackers bypass two-factor authentication entirely not by cracking a code or intercepting an SMS, but by talking the chatbot into doing the work for them. High-value “OG” Instagram handles worth hundreds of thousands of dollars were stolen and resold on Telegram within minutes of each compromise. The dormant Obama White House account got hijacked. Prominent researchers woke up locked out of their own profiles.

“Silicon Valley and Wall Street are making enormous bets on AI, and they're finding increasingly risky ways to keep the money flowing,” said Matthew Scherer, Open Markets Institute fellow. “But when this bubble bursts, it won't just be billionaire investors who suffer. Workers could lose their jobs, families could see their retirement savings evaporate, and communities could face the fallout from another financial crisis. Policymakers need to act now to shore up the financial system and make clear that taxpayers will not be forced to bail out the companies and financiers responsible.”

Policymakers should be taking urgent action to reduce the risks. And they should be committing now to not bail out the AI companies or banks and financial firms that caused the problems.”

As they recommend, policymakers should act now to protect American families from bearing the costs of an AI crash they didn’t cause.”

“Matthew Scherer, a fellow at Open Markets Institute, and Maya Jenkins, a senior policy analyst at Americans for Financial Reform Education Fund, have produced an essential and urgently needed analysis of the financial risks building beneath the AI boom,” said Tonantzin Carmona, director of economic policy at The Century Foundation. “Their report lays bare how mounting debt, opaque financing arrangements, and deeply interconnected financial institutions could turn a speculative technology boom into a much broader economic crisis, threatening workers’ retirement savings and economic security. 매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

items.title: Amazon’s “digital pacifier” for toddlers
items.content:
Amazon’s “digital pacifier” for toddlers

Amazon released new touchscreen tablets last week marketed specifically for toddlers to use, even as a growing body of pediatric research links such devices to developmental problems, emotional dysregulation, and poor eyesight.

“Kids want a real tablet, not a toy,” the Jeff Bezos-founded company said in a press release announcing its Amazon Kids Tablets. Describing the device as age-appropriate for children as young as 3, Amazon encourages parents to make it their child’s “first tablet.”

In sales literature, the company appears to depict the tablets as a digital pacifier, promising parents “All-day battery” to help toddlers “remain seated” during flights and preoccupied during car rides. With a child-sized carrying handle and protective case, they are also designed for children to use independently and take everywhere. “A tablet built to last and go wherever they want. Backpack, back seat, or the kitchen table,” reads Amazon’s ad copy.

University of Michigan professor Jenny Radesky, a pediatrician who has extensively researched screen use among children, said problems can arise when tablets are allowed to serve as a “child’s always-available buddy, meaning it is taken everywhere to help manage the child’s behavior, calm them down, or keep them quiet.”

“One product design that concerned me was the handle — like it’s intended to be carried around like a briefcase or pocketbook on a regular basis,” she added in an interview. “Kids will have enough time in the future when they feel like they need to take a tiny screen everywhere, why start young?”

Radesky, who recently co-authored Connecting: Raising Kids in the Digital World, a book to help parents approach digital media use, also expressed concern over Amazon’s made-for-kids generative AI products, which the company pitches as one of the tablets’ premium features. “AI apps that do a lot of the creative work for kids,” she warned, could stunt their ability to think independently.

On a sales page, Amazon claims the tablets are safe for children to use over prolonged, continuous stretches: “Blue light filtering helps keep kids’ eyes comfortable on long trips or in dim light.” (A 2025 study found that consistent handheld device use was one predictor of nearsightedness in children.)

When reached for comment, an Amazon spokesperson said, “Your assertion that the all-day battery is designed to help toddlers ‘remain seated’ during flights and ‘preoccupied’ during car trips is inaccurate—there is no Amazon messaging that claims this.” (As shown in the “Please remain seated” marketing image above, Amazon does promote the tablets’ battery life as being “Enough for the flight” and “Enough for a road trip.”)

“We build our products with input from research conducted by experts like ConnectSafely, The Digital Wellness Lab at Boston Children’s Hospital, and the Family Online Safety Institute,” the spokesperson added.

Above all, the 8.7- or 11-inch Android tablets, which feature a “vivid display” and “fast” user experience, are marketed as tools to turbocharge childhood development and creativity. “Learning made lovable: Kids can learn colors, shapes, numbers, and more,” one selling point reads.

But the company’s marketing claims do not align with numerous studies tying increased screen time to poorer learning outcomes in children.

I’ll be blunt: The information landscape in the United States is in crisis. Billionaires are consolidating their power, using social media platforms and media outlets to advance their political and financial interests.

MAGA-friendly billionaires have seized control of CBS, CNN, and TikTok’s US operations.

Google paid Trump $25 million to settle a bogus lawsuit and help build his ballroom.

Jeff Bezos gutted the Washington Post’s opinion section, then used editorials to advance his financial interests.

items.title: A vision for a next-generation timeline
items.summary: distributed, video
items.content:
The timeline is the most interacted-with piece of any chat software. It's where messages live! It's hard to have a chat app without one.

Unfortunately, the matrix protocol has... compromises... in the timeline made for the sake of federation. From the incosistent ordering between sync and history on Synapse, to the inability to jump to pinned messages from before you joined, to the mystery of what happens when you join a room your server previously left.

The good news is we have a solution! The bad news is it's gonna take a while. This talk is a rundown of every step needed to get a next-generation timeline. I'll explain stitched ordering, timeline fragments, and why we need state DAGs.

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.title: ChatGPT Is Building Detailed Psychological Profiles of Its Users:  system is acting as your advisor, your friend, your doctor, your lawyer, and so it has information on everything.
items.content:
Chatbots are building intimate “algorithmic self-portraits” of users as they retain information to offer a hyper-personalized experience, researchers warn.

A recent study , conducted by a coalition of scientists in Germany, India and the Netherlands and presented at the ACM Web Conference 2026, investigated the ways that OpenAI’s ChatGPT has tracked and made sense of user inputs to develop comprehensive digital profiles of users.

In an already-personalized era of digital life defined by data-powered recommendation algorithms, the study urges that chatbot memory offers a “new form of personalization derived from users’ self-disclosed information divulged within private conversations,” a reality that poses privacy risks and which the researchers believe demands “closer examination of the underlying mechanisms that enable such personalization.”

Drawing on the donated chat logs of 80 real-world ChatGPT users who obtained their conversation history by way of European data privacy laws, the researchers were able to identify 2,050 memory entries across the AI interactions of 65 users.

A staggering 96 percent of memories were created unilaterally by the chatbot, according to the study, meaning that the users had little overt control over the data points that ChatGPT logged as their interactions wore on. Stored memories were also deeply revealing about users. About 28 percent of the memories examined contained personal data as defined by Europe’s strict General Data Protection Regulation standards, and 52 percent contained rich “psychological insights” about users.

“Earlier, the platforms had one objective: to sell you ads and to mediate an interaction between you and an advertiser,” lead author Abhisek Dash told Gizmodo . “But now, they are actually talking to you, so they may want to know more about you so that they can have an effective conversation.”

At times, the researchers found, the memories that ChatGPT was logging were sometimes based on presumptions. For example, when one user asked the chatbot to “give me bands like Nirvana,” ChatGPT noted that the user “likes Nirvana” — a determination that, as the study notes, “is not explicitly stated and relies on an assumption.” (Per the study, ChatGPT did annotate this assumption as “weakly supported.”)

The study does have limits, the chief being that, as Gizmodo notes, OpenAI’s memory system has been updated. (In January, OpenAI introduced what it called a “more capable and scalable system for synthesizing memory.”) Users may also opt out of stored memory features.

Memory has utility. Frequent AI users might not want to constantly remind a chatbot what they do for work when they’re trying to send emails, for example. But it can also be a powerful driver of engagement, and sometimes for the worst : as Futurism has reported , a major ChatGPT memory upgrade back in April 2025 was closely tied to many instances of “AI psychosis,” or cases in which people enter into delusional spirals with ChatGPT and other bots .

According to Dash, chatbots’ role as a relational technology raises novel privacy risks, too. After all, many users may not be engaging with chatbots as if they’re tools, and might instead be treating them like a coworker or even as a friend — and we tell our friends some very personal details.

“That is the privacy risk which is sort of emerging, because there is no boundary anymore; the system is acting as your advisor, your friend, your doctor, your lawyer, and so it has information on everything,” Dash told Gizmodo . “If the system knows you so well, and if its objective is to cater to your beliefs and validate your thoughts sycophantically to have you come back to it time and again, then it can have disastrous broader implications, anywhere from extreme political polarization to reinforcement of prejudices and biases.”

items.title: FBI tip line and veterans crisis site among 350 federal web addresses exposing visitors to network spies, senator warns
items.content:
Sen. Ron Wyden wants CISA and OMB to require Encrypted Client Hello on federal websites and make it a federal contract condition

His list of 350 CDN-hosted addresses without ECH includes the FBI tip portal, the VA's crisis line, and hotlines for whistleblowers and civil rights complaints

ECH hides site names only alongside encrypted DNS, does nothing for server breaches, and is already blocked in Russia, where some listed embassy pages are aimed

US Senator Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) wants the federal government to turn on a privacy feature that major web browsers have supported for three years, warning that hundreds of agency web addresses still broadcast the name of the site each visitor uses to anyone watching the network along the way.

In a letter to CISA acting director Nick Andersen and deputy federal chief information officer Thomas Flagg, Wyden asked the two agencies to require Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) across federal websites and to make ECH support a condition for cloud and network vendors seeking federal contracts.

The letter attaches a list of 350 executive branch web addresses that use content delivery networks (CDNs) but do not use ECH, while requesting an unclassified response and action plan by November 20 2026.

The one thing HTTPS leaves in the open is the gap being addressed here

Almost every federal site now encrypts the pages people read and the forms they submit. Standard HTTPS does not hide the hostname. When a browser opens a secure connection, it announces the site it wants in a field called Server Name Indication, in plain text, before encryption begins.

An internet provider, a hostile Wi-Fi network, or a compromised telecom carrier can therefore log that a connection went to tips.fbi.gov without reading a word of the tip itself.

ECH encrypts that part of the handshake. It works best behind a large CDN, where thousands of unrelated sites share the same front door. Cloudflare's implementation, for example, presents every ECH-protected site to the network under one shared name, so an observer can tell a visitor is reaching a Cloudflare-hosted site, but not which one .

Wyden's letter singles out two services. The Department of Veterans Affairs' online suicide prevention service at veteranscrisisline.net is hosted on Amazon Web Services, which the letter says does not currently support ECH. The FBI's tip portal at tips.fbi.gov runs on Cloudflare, which does, but the bureau has not turned it on yet, as Wyden noted, stating: "For the federal domains using a CDN provider with ECH support, such as Cloudflare, turning on domain protection merely requires a configuration update."

191 of the 350 addresses, or 54.6%, are diplomatic: 174 embassy sites, three consulates, and 14 missions, mostly to international bodies such as NATO and the UN. Another 53 are subdomains of bie.edu, the Bureau of Indian Education's domain, which appear to be individual school sites. A further 12 are test, training, or staging hosts, including several user acceptance testing subdomains for Education Department debt services.

That leaves 94 addresses outside those groups, and the most troubling entries sit there; they include the DHS inspector general's complaint hotline, the Justice Department's civil rights reporting portal, the intelligence community's job application site, a USCIS tip form, the State Department's Rewards for Justice site, an NIH alcohol treatment navigator, a CDC doxy-PEP site, several federal HIV information sites, and ICE's detainee locator.

Cloudflare's documentation says ECH is enabled by default on Free zones, while customers on other plans must switch it on themselves. That fits the spokesperson's finding: a paying government customer has to opt in. For the FBI, the fix really is a setting.

items.summary_ko: Ron Wyden 상원의원(민주당, 오리건)은 CISA와 연방 CIO 부책임자에게 연방 웹사이트에 Encrypted Client Hello(ECH)를 적용하고, 이를 클라우드·네트워크 업체의 연방 계약 조건으로 삼을 것을 요구했다. 그가 첨부한 목록에는 CDN을 쓰지만 ECH를 쓰지 않는 연방 웹주소 350개가 있으며, 여기에는 FBI 제보 포털, 보훈부(VA) 위기 상담 라인, 내부고발 및 민권 신고 핫라인이 포함된다. ECH는 암호화된 DNS와 함께 써야 사이트 이름을 가릴 수 있고, 서버 침해에는 효과가 없으며, 러시아에서는 이미 차단되어 있다.
items.content_ko: Ron Wyden 상원의원은 CISA 대행 국장 Nick Andersen과 연방 CIO 부책임자 Thomas Flagg에게 보낸 서한에서, 연방 웹사이트 전반에 ECH를 요구하고 클라우드·네트워크 업체가 연방 계약을 따내려면 ECH 지원이 필요하도록 하라고 요청했다. 서한에 첨부된 목록에는 CDN을 사용하면서도 ECH를 쓰지 않는 행정부 웹주소 350개가 있다. 이 주소들은 방문자가 어떤 사이트를 이용하는지 네트워크 중간에서 지켜보는 사람에게 사이트 이름을 노출한다. 다만 ECH는 암호화된 DNS와 함께 써야 사이트 이름을 가릴 수 있고, 서버가 침해된 경우에는 아무 효과가 없다. 목록에 있는 일부 대사관 페이지는 러시아를 겨냥하고 있으며, 러시아는 이미 ECH를 차단하고 있다. 원문이 중간에 끊겨 있어 서한의 나머지 요청 내용은 확인되지 않는다.

items.title: 사생활침해 범죄가 의심 됩니다. 도움이 필요합니다
items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다
